Tests of the differences of a parameter between growth curves

Source: R/partest.R
partest.Rd

Compares a parameter of the population curves (random effects at zero) between the rows of newdata, e.g. the treatment levels: every row against a reference row (contrasts="dunnett", the default), or every pair of rows (contrasts="tukey"), with the tests adjusted for the number of comparisons; the summary of the fit (summary.gcTMB) gives unadjusted tests of the coefficients. For each comparison it gives the difference of the parameter on the scale of its link, its standard error from the covariance of the fixed effects, a Wald test of no difference, and a confidence interval. With b1type="rate" in gcTMB, b1 is the maximum growth rate, and partest(fit, newdata, "b1") compares the maximum growth rates.

Usage

partest(
  x,
  newdata,
  parm = "b1",
  contrasts = c("dunnett", "tukey"),
  ref = 1,
  adjust = "single-step",
  level = 0.95,
  nsim = 1e+05
)

# S3 method for class 'partest.gcTMB'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

newdata

Data frame. The values of the covariates in fform, one row for each curve to compare; the rows are named as in timeto.

parm

Character string. The parameter to compare, "b1" to "b5"

contrasts

Character string. The comparisons: "dunnett" (default) for each row of newdata against the reference row ref, or "tukey" for all the pairs of rows

ref

Integer or character string. The reference row of newdata for contrasts="dunnett": its position, or its name as in the row names of the result; the first row by default. Not used for contrasts="tukey"

adjust

Character string. Adjustment for the number of comparisons: "single-step" (default) for the single-step adjustment of the p-values and simultaneous confidence intervals (Tukey's or Dunnett's method, by contrasts), a method of p.adjust for adjusted p-values only, e.g. "holm", or "none"

level

Numeric between 0 and 1. The level of the confidence intervals

nsim

Integer. Number of simulations of the largest absolute test statistic for adjust="single-step"

digits

Integer. Number of significant digits

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class partest.gcTMB with a row for each comparison, named "a - b": the estimated difference a - b, its standard error, the test statistic, the p-value and the confidence limits, with the ratio and its limits for the log link.

Details

The tests use t quantiles with small-sample inference (gcTMBcontrol), and normal quantiles otherwise. The contrasts and the adjustment for the number of comparisons are separate choices, as in the multcomp package (Hothorn, Bretz and Westfall, 2008): the contrasts say which differences are tested, and the adjustment how their p-values and confidence intervals account for the number of them.

By default (adjust="single-step"), the p-values and the confidence intervals are adjusted by the single-step method, the default adjustment of summary.glht in multcomp: they use the distribution of the largest absolute test statistic of all the comparisons, given the correlations of the differences, so that the intervals cover all the differences simultaneously with probability level. For the comparisons with a reference, this is Dunnett's test, and for all the pairs, Tukey's honestly significant differences, both generalised to any covariance of the estimates. Dunnett's test controls the familywise error rate of the comparisons with the reference only, so its critical value is smaller than Tukey's for the same rows. The distribution is simulated, with nsim draws, which gives the adjusted p-values to about 0.002 for the default; the simulation has its own seed and leaves the random number generator as it was. The other methods of p.adjust, e.g. "holm", adjust the p-values only, and the confidence intervals are then not adjusted; "none" gives the unadjusted Wald tests.

For a parameter with the log link, the differences are log ratios, and the ratios with their confidence limits are given as well. Whether all the curves have the same value of the parameter is tested by a likelihood ratio test of the models with and without the covariates of the parameter, see anova.gcTMB. With treatment contrasts in fform and the levels in newdata in the order of the factor, the differences to the first level are the coefficients of the parameter in the summary of the fit, and adjust="none" gives their unadjusted tests of the summary.

References

Dunnett, C. W. (1955). A multiple comparison procedure for comparing several treatments with a control. Journal of the American Statistical Association 50, 1096-1121.

Hothorn, T., Bretz, F. and Westfall, P. (2008). Simultaneous inference in general parametric models. Biometrical Journal 50, 346-363.

Examples

FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
# b1 as the maximum growth rate, on the log scale: differences of log rates
fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, data=FabaHeights25, b1type="rate", link=c(b1="log"))
nd <- data.frame(trt=levels(FabaHeights25$trt))
# each treatment against the first level, by Dunnett's method
partest(fit, newdata=nd, parm="b1")
#> Differences to the reference of b1 (maximum growth rate) on the scale of its log link:
#> 
#>                   Estimate Std.Error t value p.value    lower  upper ratio
#> trt=0.3 - trt=0.1 -0.00614    0.0319  -0.193  0.9990 -0.08472 0.0724 0.994
#> trt=0.5 - trt=0.1  0.08075    0.0323   2.502  0.0456  0.00116 0.1603 1.084
#> trt=0.6 - trt=0.1  0.08555    0.0327   2.617  0.0337  0.00492 0.1662 1.089
#> trt=0.8 - trt=0.1  0.06441    0.0332   1.940  0.1640 -0.01749 0.1463 1.067
#>                   ratio.lower ratio.upper
#> trt=0.3 - trt=0.1       0.919        1.08
#> trt=0.5 - trt=0.1       1.001        1.17
#> trt=0.6 - trt=0.1       1.005        1.18
#> trt=0.8 - trt=0.1       0.983        1.16
#> 
#> Wald t tests on 189 degrees of freedom; p-values and confidence limits adjusted by the single-step (Dunnett) method, 95% confidence limits, and ratios.
# all the pairs, by Tukey's method
partest(fit, newdata=nd, parm="b1", contrasts="tukey")
#> Pairwise differences of b1 (maximum growth rate) on the scale of its log link:
#> 
#>                   Estimate Std.Error t value p.value   lower     upper ratio
